title: Against the market baseline, the skill score is negative everywhere
headline_insight: The model's Brier Skill Score versus the market is negative across every sport -- MLB overall -0.1502, soccer -0.5967 -- so the model does not beat the market, and that null is the exhibit's whole point.
what_it_means: Brier Skill Score is 1 minus Brier over a reference Brier; positive means you beat the reference. Against climatology (a constant base-rate guess) the model scores positive (MLB +0.042), as any real in-game model should. Against the market it is negative across all sports and checkpoints -- the market's Brier is lower. This is reported plainly, not hidden.
how_to_read: Read each cell's BSS: above 0 beats the baseline, below 0 loses to it; compare the vs-market column (the hard test) against the vs-climatology column (the easy one).
why_it_matters: It is the cleanest single statement of the project thesis -- the market is efficient; the model crushes the base rate but does not out-predict the market.
caveat: The most negative MLB cell is late(inn7+) at -0.4635; late-game is exactly where market prices sharpen on information the model cannot see.

cited.value: BSS vs market is near or below 0 across sports and checkpoints -- the model does not beat the market's Brier.
